title: Order book matching
summary: Implement limit-order matching: the crossing rules, two heaps, price-time priority with a map of deques, and O(1) cancel with tombstones.

clips.title: The matching rules
clips.question: An order arrives. Which resting orders does it trade with, and how much?

scenes.say: Order book, problem one. An order arrives at a limit order book. Which resting orders does it trade with, and how much does each one fill? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: An order arrives. Who does it trade with, and how much?

scenes.say: A buy trades with the cheapest resting sell, as long as that price is at or below the buy's limit. Here comes a buy for six at twelve. The best ask is eleven, where order two fills three, then order three fills two. Eleven is used up, so the buy moves up to twelve, and takes one from order one, which keeps its place with three left. Now a sell for four at eleven. The best bid is ten, below its limit, so nothing trades, and the whole order rests in the book.

steps.note: BUY 6 @ 12 sweeps the asks from the lowest price up
SELL 4 @ 11: best bid 10 < 11, so it rests

scenes.say: So, four rules. Price priority: the best opposite price trades first. A trade happens only while prices cross. Each fill is the smaller of the two quantities. And whatever is left of the incoming order rests in the book.

items.label: Priority
items.title: Best price first
items.body: Lowest ask for a buy, highest bid for a sell.

items.label: Condition
items.title: Only while crossing
items.body: BUY: ask ≤ limit. SELL: bid ≥ limit.

items.label: Quantity
items.title: min(a, b)
items.body: A partly filled resting order keeps its place.

items.label: Leftover
items.title: Rests
items.body: The remainder joins its own side of the book.

clips.title: Two heaps
clips.question: Which data structure gives you the best bid and best ask fast?

scenes.say: Problem two. To return the total quantity filled, which data structure gives you the best bid and the best ask quickly? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: Which structure gives the best bid and best ask fast?

scenes.say: Keep each side in a heap. Buys go in a max-heap, so its top is the best bid. Sells go in a min-heap, so its top is the best ask. For an incoming buy, loop while the best ask crosses its limit. Pop it, and fill the smaller of the two quantities. If the resting order was only partly filled, push its remainder back. Whatever is left of the buy rests on the buy side. Each fill costs log n, so an order with k fills is O of k log n.

props.title: A max-heap and a min-heap

highlights.note: Best bid = top of a max-heap
Best ask = top of a min-heap (greater<>)
Match while the best ask crosses
Partial fill: push the remainder back

scenes.say: Four bugs to avoid. Forgetting to push back a partial fill silently loses quantity. Using the default priority queue for sells gives you a max-heap: the wrong order. Flipping the crossing comparison matches orders that should never trade. And modifying the structured binding, instead of a local remaining copy.

items.label: Partial fills
items.title: Push back
items.body: The resting remainder must re-enter the heap.

items.label: Heap order
items.title: greater<> for sells
items.body: The default priority_queue is a max-heap.

items.label: Crossing
items.title: ≤ for buys
items.body: BUY: ask ≤ limit; SELL: bid ≥ limit.

items.label: Mutation
items.title: Copy qty
items.body: Track a local remaining, not the binding.

clips.title: Price-time priority
clips.question: Two buys rest at the same price. Who fills first, and why can't a heap guarantee it?

scenes.say: Problem three. Two buy orders rest at the same price. Who should fill first, and why can't a heap guarantee it? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: Two buys at the same price: who fills first?

scenes.say: Two buys rest at ten: order one arrived first, then order two. A sell for four at ten arrives. Price-time priority says the oldest order at the best price fills first: order one takes all three, and order two gets the last one, keeping one in the book.

A heap can't promise that. It pops by value, and two entries at the same price can come out in either order. So make each price level a FIFO queue, and keep the levels in a sorted map. The map's begin is the best level, and the deque's front is the oldest order there.

left.label: priority_queue
left.title: Price only
left.code:
buys.push({10, 3});   // order 1
buys.push({10, 2});   // order 2
buys.top();  // either one
left.body: Equal prices come out in no guaranteed order.

right.label: map<price, deque>
right.title: Price, then time
right.body: begin() = best level; front() = oldest order.

verdict.text: Price-time priority: sorted map + FIFO per level.

clips.title: Your turn: matchBuy
clips.question: Write matchBuy for a map-of-deques order book.

scenes.say: Your turn. With a map from price to a deque of orders, write match buy: sweep the asks while they cross the buy's limit, oldest order first, and record every trade. Pause and write it yourself.

props.question: Write matchBuy: sweep the asks while they cross, oldest first.
props.label: Your turn

scenes.say: Here is one solution. Bids sort with greater, so begin is the highest bid; asks sort ascending, so begin is the lowest ask. Add order rejects duplicate IDs, matches, and rests any remainder at its price. Match buy loops over the best ask, and stops as soon as it no longer crosses. It fills the front of the deque, the oldest order, and records a trade. A fully filled order leaves the deque, and an empty level leaves the map, otherwise begin would point at a dead level forever.

props.title: matchBuy, one solution

highlights.note: begin() is the best price on each side
Reject duplicates, match, rest the remainder
Stop when the best ask stops crossing
Fill the oldest order; log the trade
Pop filled orders; erase empty levels

clips.title: Cancel with tombstones
clips.question: How do you cancel an order by ID without searching the book?

scenes.say: Problem five. How do you cancel an order by its ID, without searching through the book? Pause and answer out loud.

props.question: Cancel by ID without searching the book?

scenes.say: Cancel order two. Instead of digging it out of its queue, record the ID in a cancelled set: it stays in the book as a tombstone. Later, a buy for four at twenty arrives. Matching reaches order two first, sees the tombstone, and simply pops it. Then order three fills two. Twenty is now empty, and twenty-one is above the limit, so the last two rest as a bid at twenty.

steps.note: BUY 4 @ 20: pop the tombstone, fill #3, rest 2

scenes.say: The code is tiny. Cancel just moves the ID from active to cancelled, in constant time. Before using the front of a level, skip cancelled drains any tombstones there. Each order is popped at most once, so the extra matching work is amortized constant.

props.title: Lazy deletion

highlights.note: Pop tombstones when matching reaches them
Each entry popped once: amortized O(1)

scenes.say: To recap. Trade at the best opposite price while prices cross, filling the smaller quantity. Two heaps give the best prices in log time. Price-time priority needs a sorted map of FIFO deques. And cancel lazily, with tombstones popped during matching.

items.text: Best opposite price first, while prices cross.
Two heaps: best bid and ask in O(log n).
Price-time priority: map of FIFO deques.
Cancel lazily; pop tombstones when matching.
